name: Somatropin (HGH)
summary: Lab-made human growth hormone, prescribed for growth hormone deficiency and certain growth disorders; distributing it for anti-aging or bodybuilding is a federal crime.
what_it_is: Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone: a 191-amino-acid protein made in E. coli bacteria with the same sequence as the growth hormone made by the pituitary gland. In children it promotes growth; in adults it shifts body composition toward more lean mass and less fat. Blood levels of IGF-1 rise during treatment. It is given by injection.

evidence.why: FDA-approved for growth hormone deficiency and several childhood growth disorders; in healthy older adults, a review of 18 small trials found small body-composition changes and more side effects.

status_us.label: FDA-approved; illegal to distribute for anti-aging
status_us.note: Approved as a prescription biologic for children with growth hormone deficiency, Prader-Willi syndrome, Turner syndrome, short stature after being born small for gestational age or idiopathic short stature, and for adults with growth hormone deficiency. Federal law (21 U.S.C. 333(e)) makes distributing it for other uses a crime punishable by up to 5 years in prison, FDA says no anti-aging, bodybuilding or athletic use has been authorized, and as a biologic it cannot be compounded under sections 503A or 503B.

benefits.claim: Improves growth in children with growth hormone deficiency, Prader-Willi syndrome, Turner syndrome, small-for-gestational-age short stature or idiopathic short stature
More lean mass and less body fat and waist size than placebo after 6 months in adults with growth hormone deficiency, maintained with continued treatment

About 2 kg more lean mass and 2 kg less fat, with no change in weight or bone density, in healthy older adults (18 small trials, 220 treated, average age 69); not an approved use, distributing it for anti-aging is illegal in the US, and the reviewers concluded it cannot be recommended

risks.risk: Swelling of the hands and feet, joint pain, limb pain, tingling and stiffness: swelling in 17.5% versus 5.1% on placebo in adults
Carpal tunnel syndrome (about 2% in adult extension studies) and, in healthy older adults, breast enlargement in men
Higher blood sugar: it can unmask impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes, and new diabetes or impaired fasting glucose was somewhat more likely in healthy older adults
Raised pressure inside the skull (intracranial hypertension), which usually resolves after stopping or lowering the dose
Growth of existing tumors, and second tumors (especially meningiomas) in childhood cancer survivors treated with head radiation
Higher death rates when given to critically ill adults after major surgery, trauma or acute respiratory failure
In children: slipped growth plate at the hip (a new limp or hip or knee pain needs checking), and faster worsening of an existing scoliosis during rapid growth
Pancreatitis, to be considered with persistent severe abdominal pain, especially in children (girls with Turner syndrome may be at greater risk)

avoid_if: Acute critical illness, such as after open-heart or abdominal surgery, major trauma or acute respiratory failure
Active proliferative or severe nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy
Prader-Willi syndrome with severe obesity, airway obstruction, sleep apnea or severe breathing problems
Past serious allergic reaction to somatropin
interactions: Glucocorticoids: replacement doses may need adjusting, and they can blunt growth in children
Insulin and other diabetes medicines: doses may need adjusting
Oral estrogen: can reduce its effect
Drugs cleared by CYP450 liver enzymes, such as sex steroids, anticonvulsants and cyclosporine: levels may change

before: Cortisol if adrenal insufficiency is possible
labs.why: The label calls for periodic glucose and thyroid checks and eye exams for raised pressure in the skull; IGF-1, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase and parathyroid hormone may rise during treatment.

studies.title: Systematic Review: The Safety and Efficacy of Growth Hormone in the Healthy Elderly
studies.people: 220 healthy older adults given growth hormone in 18 randomized study populations (average age 69)
studies.finding: Lean mass rose about 2.1 kg and fat fell about 2.1 kg with no change in weight or bone density; swelling, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome and breast enlargement were more common. The authors concluded growth hormone cannot be recommended as an anti-aging therapy.

studies.title: GENOTROPIN (somatropin) for injection: Prescribing Information
studies.people: Adults with growth hormone deficiency (placebo-controlled trials)
studies.finding: At 6 months, lean body mass rose and body fat and waist size fell versus placebo; bone density dipped at 6 months and returned to baseline by 12 months. Swelling and joint pain were the most common side effects.

ask_your_clinician: Have I been properly tested for growth hormone deficiency, and what did the tests show?
How will we watch my blood sugar, thyroid and eyes during treatment?
What are the safety and legal concerns with growth hormone used outside an approved condition?

sources.title: Import Alert 66-71: Detention Without Physical Examination of Unapproved Human Growth Hormone (HGH)

notes_for_editor: The label used is Genotropin (July 2025); other somatropin brands have similar but not identical indications (for example, brand-specific HIV wasting or short bowel syndrome indications were not checked). The label summary used gives no frequencies for intracranial hypertension, tumors or diabetes, so those are marked 'unknown'. The healthy-elderly review is from 2007 and pooled small, short trials. FDA's Import Alert 66-71 (revised April 7, 2026) states the 21 U.S.C. 333(e) restriction (up to 10 years if minors are involved) and that HGH, as a biologic, is not eligible for 503A or 503B compounding. Whether it is a controlled substance was not checked.
